title: Configuring the Zscaler Data Security Add-in for Outlook

blocks.text: To enable this feature for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

Employees are often either unaware of what constitutes sensitive information according to company policy or else they might accidentally commit policy violations as they do their day-to-day work. The Zscaler Data Security Add-in for Outlook (aka Zscaler Outlook Add-in) provides a turnkey solution that gives users real-time, contextual guidance as they compose messages within the Outlook app. The guidance users receive ensures that email content and attachments are thoroughly evaluated before messages ever leave an endpoint, eliminating surprises and maintaining a seamless and secure communication workflow.
This article provides an end-to-end overview of the steps necessary to configure and deploy the Zscaler Outlook Add-In across your organization.
Make sure the following prerequisites are met before starting the configuration process:

blocks.item: Contact Zscaler Support to enable the Zscaler Outlook Add-in in your tenant. After Zscaler Support enables the add-in for your organization, you receive a link to the XML manifest file to use when configuring the Exchange server, and an installation file for configuring Zscaler Client Connector with the specific Zscaler Endpoint DLP version necessary to enable the add-in on endpoints.
Exchange Online as the email provider
Endpoints running Microsoft Windows 11 or later
Endpoints running the Outlook Web App or New Outlook for Windows
1. Upload the manifest file to the Exchange server.
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
In the left-side navigation, go to Settings > Integrated Apps.
See image.
The Integrated apps page appears.
On the Integrated apps page, click Upload custom apps.
See image.
The Upload Apps to deploy drawer opens.
In the Upload Apps to deploy drawer, in the App type drop-down menu, select Office Add-in.
In the Choose how to upload app section, select Provide link to manifest file and add the URL previously provided by Zscaler Support, then click Validate.
See image.
You receive a confirmation message after Exchange uploads and validates the manifest file.
Click Next.
The Add users page appears.
On the Add users page, in the Assign Users section, select the users to assign to the add-in, then click Next.
See image.
To minimize interruptions in your production environment, Zscaler recommends using a phased rollout and limiting your initial implementation to a small group for testing.
The Accept permissions requests page opens.
On the Accept permissions requests page, review the App capabilities, then click Next.
The Review and finish deployment page opens.
See image.
The Deployment completed page opens after the deployment completes, and you receive a confirmation message that the add-in can take up to 72 hours to be available in Outlook.
See image.
If you selected Just me as the user option on the Add users page, or if you selected only a small number of users (i.e., 4-5 users), the add-in should be available for testing in less than an hour.
Click Done.
You return to the Integrated apps page, and the Zscaler Outlook Add-in appears in the list.
2. Add the Zscaler Outlook Add-in as an email tenant.
Configure an Exchange tenant to use the Outlook Email Add-in. To learn more, see Adding Email Tenants.
3. Install a supported version of Data Protection in Client Connector.

In Zscaler Client Connector, ensure that you have deployed the version of Endpoint DLP provided by Zscaler Support to endpoints across your organization. To learn more, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles.
4. Configure Outbound Email Policy rules to use the Outlook Email Add-in.

Configure Outbound Email Policy rules that use Outlook Add-in as the Evaluation Mode, and then apply them to the Exchange tenant you created earlier. To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules.
5. Use the Zscaler Outlook Add-in to compose email messages.
Open the Outlook app.
When you compose an email, the Zscaler Outlook Add-in appears in the Outlook Ribbon.
See image.
(Optional) Click the Zscaler Outlook Add-in button to see information about the add-in.
See image.

Compose email content that is immediately compared against your organization’s Outbound Email DLP policy. In this example, a user receives the following message when the message subject contains "Company Confidential", which is a violation of company policy.

(Optional) Click View Details to see more information about why the email was blocked.
